amendments.body: Current-schema save/load can advance newly added shrimp halfway through the molt cycle. AnimalState still defaults inter_molt_timer_days to 14.0 (crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:615), AddShrimp seeds the adult stage timer to 0 without syncing that legacy field (crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:818-823), and normalize_loaded_shrimp_reproduction_state() blindly backfills any all-zero stage timers from inter_molt_timer_days (crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:946-960). A fresh v13 save with newly added adults will therefore reload with adult.molt_timer_days = 14.0 instead of 0. Restrict that backfill to migrated pre-v13 payloads, or only run it when the stage timer fields were absent in the source JSON.
amendments.rationale: This is a real save/load correctness bug: roundtripping a current save mutates simulation state even when no migration should apply.

amendments.body: Cold-water molt failures are misreported. molt_cycle() multiplies success by temp_condition_factor() for both below- and above-optimal temperatures (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:440-441, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:504-506), but emit_molt_failure() and emit_molt_stress_warning() only add a temperature cause when temperature_c > optimal_temp_max_c (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1113-1118, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1161-1163). In a cold tank, the new mechanic can fail molts while emitting only PoorCondition, which hides the actual driver. Add an explicit low-temperature cause/detail, or at minimum include any non-optimal temperature penalty in the event summary.
amendments.rationale: The feature promise here is debuggable failure attribution; cold-induced failures currently produce misleading events.

amendments.body: Reserve depletion is part of the new success formula, but it is not surfaced in failure diagnostics. The success path feeds reserve_g into molt_condition_modifier() (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:502-503, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1258-1276), yet emit_molt_failure() only reports a raw condition index when it blames PoorCondition (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1120-1127). A reserve-driven failure can therefore log a seemingly healthy condition value with no reserve/starvation hint. Include reserve-per-shrimp or reserve shortfall in the event details, or emit a starvation/reserve cause code when that branch drives the failure.
amendments.rationale: Without this, one of the main new mechanics is effectively opaque to players and to anyone debugging a failing scenario.

amendments.body: The ‘very low GH forces failure’ cutoff is still a hidden magic threshold. CRITICAL_MOLT_GH_RATIO is hardcoded at 0.3 (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:12) and applied directly in the failure gate (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:439, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:508) instead of coming from ShrimpRuntimeParams. That leaves one of the new molt-failure boundaries untunable and without preset/provenance coverage. Promote this cutoff into named runtime/preset data, or derive it from the existing named GH parameters rather than keeping a hidden constant.
amendments.rationale: This is a significant maintainability and tuning risk, and it undercuts the stated goal that the new thresholds be inspectable and data-driven.

payload.summary: Reviewed the final mineral-budget/molting changes, read the touched runtime/save/preset files, and ran the affected tank_core test suites. The tests pass, but I found four issues: one current-schema save/load state corruption path, two gaps in molt-failure attribution, and one remaining hidden GH threshold that should be data-driven.
